features.description: Convergence-delta no_progress breaker. The no_progress breaker treats a round whose auditor findings CHANGE materially from the prior round as progress, not as a no-progress stall — extending the convergence-bugs-v2 Design B carve-out from strictly-shrinking finding COUNT to changing finding CONTENT. True no-progress (findings repeat materially unchanged across consecutive rounds) is preserved.
features.acceptance: (1) Progress is defined structurally: a round makes progress IFF at least one blocking-finding signature present in the PRIOR round is ABSENT in the current round (a prior finding was resolved), computed from compute_audit_finding_signature — never from the verdict string. (2) check_no_progress TRIPS after the configured consecutive rounds in which NO prior-round blocking-finding signature is resolved (every prior blocking signature persists), EVEN IF new, distinct findings appeared that round — new findings alone are NOT progress (this closes the infinite-churn hole: an auditor that keeps raising different problems without any being resolved still terminates). (3) 'Distinct' is set-membership of NORMALIZED per-finding signatures; a reworded-but-substantively-identical finding yields the same signature and does NOT count as progress. (4) The strictly-shrinking-count carve-out from convergence-bugs-v2 (D003 Design B) is a special case of (1) and is preserved. (5) Red tests cover: prior-finding-resolved -> no trip; nothing-resolved-but-new-findings-appeared -> trips; reworded-identical-finding -> trips. (6) Every existing circuit_breakers / supervisor convergence test stays green.
steps: Red test first: a 2-round fixture where round N and N+1 carry DISTINCT blocking findings must NOT terminate no_progress; a fixture where they repeat unchanged MUST terminate.
Read circuit_breakers.check_no_progress, compute_audit_finding_signature, and the convergence-bugs-v2 Design B carve-out (2026-05-30-002 F001).
Make check_no_progress compute progress from the finding-content signature delta across rounds, not the verdict string.
Preserve the strictly-shrinking-count carve-out and the materially-unchanged path.
Run the full circuit_breakers + supervisor convergence test modules (local pytest).

features.description: First-class operator-finish close path. `dontpanic close` accepts honest terminal classes beyond stopped_no_progress — signed-off-adjacent (auditor signed off but a downstream gate blocked, e.g. patch-completeness on untracked files), staging-blocked, and operator-verified — closing them with a recorded, accurate signoff_reason instead of forcing a stopped_no_progress / breaker:no_progress pretence. Closing writes clear evidence and triggers no paid dispatch.
features.acceptance: (1) ANTI-BYPASS: the signed_off_adjacent class REFUSES to close unless the latest auditor envelope's verdict is actually signed_off — it cannot relabel a needs_changes / failed audit as operator-resolved (a red test asserts refusal when the latest verdict is needs_changes). (2) With a real signed_off envelope, `dontpanic close --operator-resolved --reason signed_off_adjacent` closes WITHOUT requiring breaker:no_progress to be active and WITHOUT recording the close as stopped_no_progress. (3) staging_blocked requires a recorded downstream-gate block (e.g. patch_completeness) as its evidence; operator_verified records the operator-supplied rationale and what was verified. (4) The signoff envelope's signoff_reason and the closeout memo record the ACTUAL terminal class, never a no-progress pretence. (5) The close path performs no paid agent dispatch (a test asserts no executor is invoked). (6) The existing stopped_no_progress close behavior is unchanged.
steps: Red test first: a signed-off-adjacent terminal (signoff present, patch-completeness blocked, breaker:no_progress NOT active) closes via the CLI and writes an accurate signoff_reason.
Read the close CLI + closeout / signoff_writer + the breaker-active safety check.
Add the honest terminal classes + reasons; relax the breaker-active precondition for them while keeping the stopped_no_progress path intact.
Assert the close path invokes no executor (no paid dispatch).
Run the close / closeout / signoff test modules (local pytest).

features.description: Patch-completeness untracked-module gap. The patch-completeness gate surfaces an untracked IMPLEMENTATION module (e.g. a new plan_review/sizing_gate.py imported by the change) alongside an untracked test, so a fresh clone neither fails to run a test nor import-fails on a missing module — while continuing to ignore unrelated generated/runtime output (the standing onboarding-v0 noise) rather than reporting it broadly.
features.acceptance: (1) RELEVANCE is defined structurally: an untracked path is a completeness blocker IFF it is (a) within the dispatch's touched set OR (b) a first-party module imported by a file the dispatch adds or modifies — NOT a blanket untracked-file scan. (2) When a dispatch adds an untracked test AND an untracked implementation module imported by a changed file, the gate surfaces BOTH (the F007 sizing_gate.py case where only the test was reported). (3) Unrelated untracked generated/runtime output (evidence/audit artifacts, pre-existing noise outside the touched/imported set) is NOT reported as a completeness blocker. (4) A red test reproduces the F007 untracked-module miss and asserts it is surfaced; a negative test asserts an unrelated untracked runtime file (outside the touched/imported set) is NOT flagged.
steps: Red test first: a change adding an untracked module imported by the change is surfaced; an unrelated untracked runtime file is not.
Read patch_completeness_gate's untracked-file detection + how it scopes to the change.
Extend detection to the change's imported/implementation modules, scoped to the touched set.
Keep unrelated generated/runtime output out of the report.
Run the patch_completeness test module (local pytest).
